# Spinal muscular atrophy

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Neurology > Neuromuscular disorders > Spinal muscular atrophy*

[Original Article Link](/library/MR0Mnf)

---

## Summary

Spinal muscular <u>atrophy</u> (SMA) refers to a group of <u>autosomal recessive</u> motor <u>neuron</u> diseases that are caused by <u>apoptosis</u> of <u>lower motor neurons</u>. Patients typically present during <u>infancy</u> or early childhood with progressive <u>weakness</u>, <u>hypotonia</u>, muscle <u>atrophy</u>, <u>hyporeflexia</u>/areflexia, and varying degrees of bulbar <u>weakness</u>. The severity of disease is related to the age of onset; <u>type 1 SMA</u> (<u>Werdnig-Hoffmann disease</u>) is associated with <u>death</u> within the first two years of life as a result of respiratory muscle <u>paralysis</u> or <u>aspiration pneumonia</u>. With other types of SMA, children usually survive to adulthood, but motor milestones may be delayed and <u>joint contractures</u> and/or deformities of the <u>spine</u> can occur. The diagnosis is confirmed by <u>genetic testing</u>. In 2016, the <u>FDA</u> approved the use of <u>nusinersen</u>, which is highly effective in halting the progression of SMA; in 2019, <u>onasemnogene abeparvovec</u>, a potentially curative genetic therapy, was approved. Supportive therapy is aimed at preventing respiratory and orthopedic complications.

---

## Etiology

* <u>Autosomal recessive</u>: defect in the SMN1 <u>gene</u> on <u>chromosome</u> 5q:   → defect in the assembly of <u>small nuclear ribonucleoprotein</u> (<u>snRNP</u>) to form the SMN complex → <u>apoptosis</u> of <u>lower motor neurons</u> (especially the <u>anterior horn cells</u> in the spinal cord) in the later stages of <u>fetal development</u> and postnatal period

---

## Pathophysiology

* Congenital motor <u>neuron</u> disease that only involves the <u>lower motor neurons</u> (spinal ± bulbar motor <u>neurons</u>) → <u>muscle weakness</u>, <u>hypotonia</u>, bulbar symptom

* Sensations are not affected

* Motor <u>neurons</u> of <u>cranial</u> nerves III, IV, and VI, and sacral motor <u>neurons</u> are not affected → preserved <u>eye</u> movement and continence

---

| Type of SMA | Type 0 SMA | <u>Type I SMA</u> (Werdnig-Hoffmann disease) | Type II SMA | <u>Type III SMA</u> (Kugelberg-Welander disease) | Type IV SMA (adult SMA) |
| <br><u>Proportion</u> of all SMA cases [[2]](/library/kf1mmT0) | <br>* < 1%<br><br> | <br>* ∼ 55%<br><br> | <br>* ∼ 30%<br><br> | <br>* ∼ 15%<br><br> | <br>* < 1%<br><br> |
| Severity | <br>* Very severe<br><br> | <br>* Severe<br><br> | <br>* Intermediate<br><br> | <br>* Mild<br><br> | <br>* Mild<br><br> |
| Age of onset | <br>* Prenatal<br><br> | <br>* 0–6 months<br><br> | <br>* 7–18 months<br><br> | <br>* > 18 months<br><br> | <br>* 10–30 years<br><br> |
| Typical features | <br><br>* Prenatal: absent or decreased fetal movements<br><br>* At <u>birth</u> [[3]](/library/bf1HkT0)<br><br>* Severe <u>muscle weakness</u> and <u>hypotonia</u><br><br>* <u>Respiratory failure</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Severe <u>muscle weakness</u> (<u>flaccid paralysis</u>) and <u>infantile hypotonia</u> (frog-leg posture)<br><br>* Symmetrical involvement of <u>proximal</u> muscles, mostly of the lower extremities<br><br>* <u>Intercostal muscle</u> <u>weakness</u> → <u>paradoxical breathing</u><br><br>* Upper <u>cranial nerves</u> are not affected.<br><br>* Diminished or absent <u>deep tendon reflexes</u><br><br>* Severe <u>bulbar palsy</u><br><br>* <u>Respiratory failure</u><br><br>* <u>Atrophy</u> and <u>fasciculations</u> of the <u>tongue</u><br><br>* <u>Fasciculations</u> of the fingers<br><br>* Weak cry and <u>cough</u><br><br>* Inability to swallow → difficulty feeding, drooling, ↑ risk of <u>aspiration</u><br><br>* Recurrent <u>hip dislocation</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Fine hand <u>tremors</u><br><br>* Delayed motor milestones<br><br>* Poor weight gain<br><br>* Weak <u>cough</u><br><br>* Musculoskeletal abnormalities<br><br>* <u>Joint contractures</u><br><br>* <u>Hip dislocation</u><br><br>* <u>Kyphosis</u><br><br>* <u>Scoliosis</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Variable degree of <u>muscle weakness</u><br><br>* Cramps, muscle aches<br><br>* <u>Joint</u> <u>pain</u><br><br><br> |  |
| Motor milestones | <br>* Typically, none are achieved<br><br> | <br>* Never sits<br><br> | <br>* Able to sit independently, but cannot stand without support<br><br> | <br>* Able to stand and walk independently<br><br> |  |
| <u>Life expectancy</u> | <br>* < 6 months<br><br> | <br>* < 2 years<br><br> | <br>* Approx. 30 years<br><br> | <br>* Near normal <u>life expectancy</u><br><br> |  |





> [!TIP]
> The most common <u>causes of death</u> in individuals with SMA are <u>respiratory insufficiency</u> (due to <u>respiratory muscle weakness</u>) and <u>aspiration pneumonia</u> (due to bulbar <u>weakness</u>).




> [!TIP]
> The later the age of onset, the better the prognosis.




> [!NOTE]
> Type I → non-sitters, type II → sitters, type III → walkers

---

## Diagnosis

* <u>Genetic testing</u>: best initial and <u>confirmatory test</u>

* Further tests 

* Muscle <u>biopsy</u>: <u>atrophy</u> of groups of <u>motor units</u> interspersed with normal or <u>hypertrophied</u> <u>motor units</u>

* <u>EMG</u>: spontaneous, large-amplitude, low-frequency electrical activity (<u>rarified interference pattern</u>)

* Laboratory tests: normal or mildly elevated <u>creatine kinase</u>

---

## Differential diagnoses

* Congenital myasthenic syndromes: <u>muscle weakness</u> induced by fatigue, <u>ptosis</u>, <u>extraocular muscle</u> palsy

* Congenital <u>myopathies</u>: more prominent <u>hypotonia</u> and <u>weakness</u> in <u>proximal</u> muscles

* Certain viral infections (<u>polio</u>, <u>coxsackievirus</u>, <u>echovirus</u>, <u>West Nile virus</u>): much more acute onset of <u>flaccid paralysis</u>, ascending <u>paralysis</u> (i.e., starts distally)

* Hypotonic <u>cerebral palsy</u> : non-progressive <u>weakness</u>

* <u>Muscular dystrophies</u> : ↑↑ <u>creatine kinase</u>, characteristic findings on muscle <u>biopsy</u>

* Rare juvenile form of <u>amyotrophic lateral sclerosis</u>: predominantly bulbar <u>weakness</u> with minimal involvement of <u>anterior horn cells</u>

* Motor <u>neuron</u> degeneration: associated with severe <u>arthrogryposis</u>

* <u>Progressive muscular atrophy</u>: a nonhereditary, adult-onset, progressive <u>lower motor neuron</u> disorder




The differential diagnoses listed here are not exhaustive.

---

## Treatment

* Definitive therapy [[1]](/library/g2YFSo)

* Nusinersen

* An <u>antisense</u> <u>nucleotide</u> that alters differential <u>splicing</u> of the transcript of the SMN2 <u>gene</u>, so it produces a functional SMN1 protein

* Requires annual intrathecal injections

* Onasemnogene abeparvovec 

* An agent based on an adeno-associated <u>virus</u> 9-based <u>vector</u> that carries a normal copy of SMN1 to the <u>lower motor neurons</u> of the spinal cord

* Should be administered intravenously once in a lifetime

* Risdiplam

* <u>mRNA</u> <u>splicing</u> modulator that improves the efficiency of SMN2 <u>gene</u> <u>transcription</u> → ↑ systemic SMN protein concentration

* Can be given orally, in contrast to <u>nusinersen</u>

* Supportive therapy

* <u>Respiratory support</u>

* <u>Nutritional support</u>

* Physical <u>rehabilitation</u>

* <u>Orthotics</u> to prevent <u>joint</u> and <u>spine</u> deformities
